paragraphs.en: Human {speech} contains more than 2,000 different sounds, from the common “m” and “a” to the rare {clicks} of some {southern} {African} languages.But why are certain sounds more common than others? A {ground-breaking} , five-year study shows that {diet} -related changes in human {bite} led to new speech sounds that are now found in half the world's languages.
paragraphs.cn: 人类 <u> 语言 </u> 包含2000多种不同的声音，从常见的“m”和“a”到 <u> 非洲南部 </u> 某些语言中罕见的 <u> 吸气音 </u> 。但为什么某些声音比其他声音更常见呢？一项历时五年的 <u> 开拓性 </u> 研究表明，人类因 <u> 饮食 </u> 导致的 <u> 咬合 </u> 变化催生了新的发音，而这些发音如今已存在于世界上一半的语言之中。

paragraphs.en: Cultural factors have received {priority} in language studies as their influences might seem {straightforward} .However, speech sounds can change in a rather {passive} way.More than 30 years ago, the scholar Charles Hockett noted that speech sounds called labiodentals ( (唇齿音) ), such as “f” and “v”，were more {typical} in the languages of societies that ate softer foods.Now a team of researchers led by Damián Blasi at the University of Zurich, Switzerland, has found how and why this trend {arose} .
paragraphs.cn: 语言研究向来 <u> 优先 </u> 考虑文化因素，因为它们的影响看似 <u> 直观明了 </u> 。然而，语音可以以一种相当 <u> 被动的 </u> 方式发生变化。30多年前，学者查尔斯·霍克特就注意到，在食用较软食物的社会，诸如“f”和“v”的唇齿音在其语言中更为 <u> 常见 </u> 。现在，瑞士苏黎世大学的达米安·布拉西带领的研究团队发现了这一趋势的 <u> 产生 </u> 过程和原因。

paragraphs.en: They discovered that the {arches} of upper and lower front teeth of ancient human adults were aligned ( (对齐) ), making it hard for the {speakers} to produce labiodentals, which are formed by touching the lower lip to the upper teeth.Later, our {jaws} changed to an overbite ( (上包齿) ) {structure} , making it easier to produce such sounds, which is also why {abnormal} bite patterns like underbite ( (反颌) ) or crowded teeth would lead to unclear pronunciation of certain sounds.
paragraphs.cn: 他们发现，古代成年人的上下门牙 <u> 牙弓 </u> 是相互对齐的，这使得 <u> 说话者 </u> 很难发出下唇碰触上齿形成的唇齿音。后来，我们的 <u> 颌骨 </u> 演变成了上包齿 <u> 结构 </u> ，从而更容易发出唇齿音，这也解释了为何反颌或牙齿拥挤等 <u> 异常 </u> 咬合模式会导致某些发音不清晰。

paragraphs.en: The team showed that this change in bite was connected with the {development} of agriculture in the Neolithic period.Food became easier to {chew} at this point.We didn't have to eat {rough} food like {bamboo} and {raw} {meat} anymore.The {jawbone} didn't have to do as much work and so didn't grow to be so large.The advent ( (出现) ) of food processing brought about {finer} food like {bread} and {rice} , {prompting} the {accommodation} of our {organ} structures even further.
paragraphs.cn: 该团队发现，这种咬合方式的变化与新石器时代的农业 <u> 发展 </u> 有关。在这一时期，食物变得更容易 <u> 咀嚼 </u> 了。我们不必再吃 <u> 竹子 </u> 、 <u> 生肉 </u> 等 <u> 粗硬的 </u> 食物。 <u> 下颚骨 </u> 无需再承担那么多咀嚼工作，因此也就不会长得那么大了。食品加工业的出现带来了 <u> 面包 </u> 、 <u> 米饭 </u> 等更 <u> 精细的 </u> 食物，进一步 <u> 促使 </u> 我们的 <u> 器官 </u> 结构做出 <u> 适应 </u> 性变化。

paragraphs.en: {Subsequent} {analysis} of a language {database} also confirmed that there was a global change in the sound of languages after the Neolithic age, with the use of “f” and “v” increasing {remarkably} during the last few thousand years.These sounds are still not found in the languages of many hunter-gatherer ( (狩猎采集者) ) peoples today.
paragraphs.cn: 对语言 <u> 数据库 </u> 的 <u> 后续分析 </u> 也证实，新石器时代之后，各种语言的发音发生了全球性的变化。在过去几千年里，“f”和“v”的使用 <u> 显著 </u> 增加。如今，在许多狩猎采集者群体所使用的语言中，仍然找不到这些音。

paragraphs.en: This research {overturns} the popular view that all human speech sounds were present when human beings evolved around 300,000 years ago.“The set of speech sounds we use has not necessarily remained {stable} since the appearance of human beings, but rather the {huge} variety of speech sounds that we find today is the product of a complex {interplay} of things like {biological} change and cultural evolution,”said Steven Moran, a member of the research team.
paragraphs.cn: 这项研究 <u> 推翻 </u> 了广为流行的观点，即大约30万年前，人类经由演化诞生之时，所有人类语音就已经存在。研究团队的成员史蒂文·莫兰说：“自人类出现以来，我们使用的语音体系不一定总是保持 <u> 稳定 </u> ，相反，我们如今所发现的种类 <u> 繁 </u> 多的语音是 <u> 生物 </u> 变化和文化演进等诸多复杂因素 <u> 相互作用 </u> 的产物。” 5NoOncib/NjiX02BpMIzP4m+378Hw1xTRxUdPaP/PFjKUFq4K2G7tp6ZLYoCE601yW1W39VMdLmovFdSHs4nVQ==
